description: A 23-dimension evaluation suite for instruction-driven time series forecasting systems. Dimensions are organized into five capability groups: forecasting, temporal reasoning, instruction following, uncertainty, and efficiency. The suite combines public time series sources and task-specific instruction templates across energy, transportation, weather, finance, healthcare, retail, and monitoring domains.

paired_evaluation.purpose: All compared systems, ablations, and baselines must use the same selected sample identifiers.

D1_short_term_forecasting.description: Multi-domain short-horizon forecasting across 9 datasets with horizons of 24–96 steps

D2_long_horizon.description: Long-horizon forecasting up to 720 steps, testing degradation under extended prediction windows

D3_multivariate.description: Simultaneous multi-channel prediction requiring joint modeling of correlated time series

D4_zero_shot.description: Cross-domain zero-shot transfer: model trained on source domain, tested on unseen target domain

D5_few_shot.description: Few-shot learning with 5%–100% training data availability, measuring data efficiency

D6_trend_judgment.description: Binary and multi-class trend direction assessment (rising/falling/stable) with calibrated thresholds

D7_anomaly_reasoning.description: Anomaly detection and type classification (spike, level shift, trend break, noise burst) with root cause analysis

D8_periodicity.description: Periodicity identification: detecting cycle lengths and verifying estimated periods against ground truth

D9_robustness.description: Robustness to perturbations: missing values, noise injection, and distribution shifts

D10_uncertainty.description: Uncertainty quantification via P10/P50/P90 prediction intervals with coverage and calibration metrics

D11_instruction_following.description: Strict JSON format compliance, field completeness, and extra-field detection under varied instruction formats

D12_multi_turn.description: Multi-turn dialogue with iterative prediction refinement, clarification, and follow-up analysis

D13_causal_reasoning.description: Causal attribution: identifying primary and secondary drivers (holiday, weather, policy, seasonal) of observed patterns

D14_solar.description: Renewable energy forecasting: solar plant output and hydroelectric generation with zero-inflated diurnal patterns

D15_uea_classification.description: Time series classification across UEA/UCR/MONSTER benchmarks: gesture, activity, sensor, and medical signals

D16_agent_capability.description: Autonomous agent workflow: multi-step planning, tool orchestration, and dependency-aware task decomposition

D17_missing_robustness.description: Robustness under progressive data missingness (10%–90%), measuring degradation slope and recovery behavior

D18_efficiency.description: Inference efficiency benchmarking: latency, throughput, GPU memory, and token budget compliance across varying load

D19_multivar_attribution.description: Multi-variable attribution: ranking input channels by predictive contribution and detecting spurious correlations

D20_horizon_degradation.description: Systematic horizon degradation analysis: sMAPE growth rate as prediction length increases from 12 to 336 steps

D21_comprehensive_score.description: End-to-end comprehensive assessment combining prediction accuracy, reasoning depth, and explanation quality

D22_outlier_robustness.description: Robustness to extreme outliers: NAB benchmark perturbations with error increase, recovery time, and stability scoring

D23_multi_turn_conversation.description: Extended multi-turn conversational forecasting with consistency tracking across 4+ follow-up turns

data_sources: ETT (4 variants) / Electricity / Traffic / Weather / Exchange Rate / Illness / M5 Retail / Solar / NAB / UEA / UCR / MONSTER / MSL / SMAP / SMD / PSM / SWaT / Yahoo S5
release_note: The full suite contains 8,120 source instances. Reported paired evaluations use the fixed manifest unless a paper explicitly states another manifest.
